title: Is reddit dead for marketing?
author: Tom_Baron
selftext:
It seems all the game dev subs are absolutely flooded with bitterness and spite. You cant get a post off anywhere, promo or discussion even without a tonne of down votes for no reason 

I posted two almost ideantical videos of my game on a niche sub two months apart and got 100 upvotes the first time and 0 the second. 

Further to this there are people just setting out using AI posting on solodev etc and getting burned down instantly. A flood of posts. People in subs simply replying slop despite games not clearly being ai at all. Its all very toxic

Ive got a plan for mine and it doesnt involve reddit. Have any of you had the same thoughts recently?

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body:
Your post was automatically removed because it looks like it's mainly about anti-AI attitudes elsewhere, without discussing game development using AI. This sub is focused on game development using generative AI (Rule 1).

A mod will review this removal and can restore the post if it was a mistake. You don't need to do anything, but you can [message the mods](https://www.reddit.com/message/compose?to=/r/aigamedev) if you want to add context.

comments.author: advanced_peeling
comments.body: I think cause at this point its just as seeing a pebble on a beach filled with almost identical pebbles.

comments.author: SadMangonel
comments.body:
Reddit is still one of the biggest internet communities for all kinds of gaming. 

Its hard to say without a link to your game or to the posts you mentioned. Youre saying your post got 0 upvotes, but that would also apply to a bad game.

replies.author: Tom_Baron
replies.body: My example is just a tiny observation amongst it all as the difference two months can make.

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
I don't know if it is just reddit, in any case this is temporary. I know many developers in many different companies and all use AI by now.  
This is business software development,  but I guess that the same is true for gamedev.

So, in short time, it will be very rare to not use AI.
